3.0 ARCHITECTURE

3.1 Layers and call rules

V2 has five layers. A layer may call only the layers below it. Data, not calls, crosses upward.

[[FIG structure_chart | Structure chart: the layers and who may call whom]]
LayerContentsMay callMust not
5 ScreensTabs, panels, menus built from the commands table, the canvas element4, 3 (read only), 2 (render)change a document except through a command
4 CommandsThe commands table; each command takes a document and returns a new one3, 1touch the page or the canvas
3 Documents and sessionDocument model, point table, evaluation, session state, history1paint, or know about tabs
2 Renderers and outputCanvas, SVG, PDF, nail list, thumbnails1 (types only)evaluate geometry, read session
1 Kernel and generatorsPaths, makers, shapers, connectors, finders; generator filesnothing aboveuse the page, the canvas, time, randomness without a seed, or any state
DR-3.1A check (part of the import check, FR-6.17) shall read every module's imports and fail if a module imports from a layer above its own. Layer is given by folder.
DR-3.2The Node service is outside the layers; only the storage module of layer 3 and the catalog may call it, through named requests (section 9).

3.2 Folders

sketchpad/
  kernel/        paths.js, makers/, shapers/, connectors/, finders/      layer 1, pure
  generators/    one file per generator (circle.js, parabola.js, lattice.js ...)
  templates/     one file per template (rectangle.js, ruler.js ...)
  documents/     model.js, points.js, evaluate.js, migrate.js, checks.js   layer 3
  session/       session.js, history.js
  commands/      table.js, one file per family (layers.js, points.js, sweep.js ...)
  render/        canvas.js, svg.js, pdf.js, nails.js, thumbnails.js       layer 2
  screens/       one folder per tab, plus panels/ and menus.js            layer 5
  host/          the script host (iframe page and adapter)
  service/       the Node service (requests, watcher, paths)
  library/       the owner's content: figures/, scripts/, ideabook/, help/
  journal/       journals, one file per item (section 14)
  tests/         regression/, kernel/, service/, screens/
  vendor/        outside libraries, pinned

Library content is kept apart from code so that the code can be replaced, and the content kept, without mixing the two.

4.0 THE KERNEL

4.1 Types

// A point. z defaults to 0 (D-11).
Point   = { x: number, y: number, z?: number }

// A path: points in order, and whether the last joins the first.
Path    = { pts: Point[], closed: boolean, name?: string }

// A stitch: one thread, from a to b. src names where each end came from.
Stitch  = { a: Point, b: Point, src?: { pathA: string, i: number, pathB: string, j: number } }

// What a generator returns. Nothing in it is a function; it can be saved as JSON.
Geometry = {
  paths:    { [name: string]: Path },     // the infrastructure: where nails can go
  stitches: Stitch[],                     // the threads
  points:   { [name: string]: Point },    // named points: handles, features
  bounds:   { x0, y0, x1, y1 },
  style:    { color, lineWidth, alpha? }  // per stitch overrides allowed: Stitch.style
}
DR-4.1Kernel functions shall take values and return new values; they shall never change their arguments. A test shall freeze every argument (Object.freeze, deeply) and call each kernel function with it.
DR-4.2Kernel functions shall not read window, document, a canvas, the clock, or Math.random. Randomness comes from a seed argument through the kernel's own generator (DR-4.12).
DR-4.3Every kernel function shall have defaults for every setting (D-15), and shall return a result for any input of the right type, however odd, except where the result is undefined (a path of zero points cannot be joined), in which case it returns an empty result and a note (DR-4.4), never throws.
DR-4.4A kernel function may return notes beside its value: { value, notes: ["arm 2 has 12 points, arm 1 has 20: joined the first 12"] }. Notes are shown in the layer's status, not as errors.

4.2 Makers

A maker returns a path. Signature: maker(settings) → Path. Settings are listed with their defaults.

MakerSettings (default)Result
linea {0,0}, b {100,0}, n 10n+1 evenly spaced points, open
circlecenter {0,0}, r 100, ry = r, n 24, start -90°, turn 0°, spacing "angle" | "arc"n points, closed. "arc" spaces evenly by arc length (V1's createNodes), which matters for ellipses
arccenter, r 100, from 0°, to 180°, n 10n+1 points, open
polygoncenter, r 100, sides 3, perSide 10, turn 0°points along the edges, corners once each, closed
starcenter, R 100, r 40, n 5, turn 0°2n corners, tips at R, notches at r, closed
zigzagcenter, width 500, height 150, teeth 62·teeth+1 corners, open
spiralcenter, r0 10, r1 200, turns 3, n 120, kind "archimedean" | "log"n+1 points, open
parametricfx(t), fy(t) as expressions, t0, t1, n, sampling "even-t" | "even-length" | "adaptive"see 4.6
roulettecenter, R 150, r 52 (negative: outside), d 60, turns 13, steps 600, dChange 0 per turnhypotrochoid or epitrochoid; dChange varies the pen distance as it draws (FR-6.19.4)
pointspts: Point[]the given points (for hand-placed nails)

4.4 Connectors

A connector takes one or two paths and returns stitches: connector(a, b?, settings) → Stitch[]. The family is pluggable (FR-6.2.5a): each connector is a file in kernel/connectors/. Notation: ai is point i of path a, na its length.

ConnectorRuleSettings (default)Notes
pairwiseai – bi+offset for i = from, from+every, … < tooffset 0, every 1, from 0, to na, reverse false (b run backwards), wrap falseV1's stitcher is offset 0; past b's end without wrap: stop, with a note
cornerpairwise on line(a→c, n) and line(c→b, n)a, c, b, n 15the classic curve stitch
skipai – a(i+s) mod ns 1, wrap true, from, toreplaces V1's three chord functions
growingSkipai – around(i + s0 + i·g) mod ns0 30, g 0.4curls and teardrops (14 of the owner's boards)
timesTableai – around(i·k) mod n, skipping j = ik 2 (negative and fractional allowed)k=2 cardioid, 3 nephroid, −2 deltoid, −1 parallel chords
allPairsai – aj, i < j—Mystic Rose; n(n−1)/2 stitches: budget-checked
ringai – ai+1closedoutlines
mirrorai – an−1−i—
linkedamong several paths, by link style pairwise | ring | allstyle "pairwise"Linked Circles
fanevery ai to one point ppbursts, cones, wheels
[[FIG connectors_figure | Connectors: four ways of joining the same points]]
DR-4.5Each stitch shall carry src: the path names and indices of its two ends. Printing (nail numbering, colour cycle FR-6.11.9) and hit-testing read it.
DR-4.6When two paths of different lengths are joined pairwise, the default shall be to join the shorter's length and note it; a setting match: "resample" resamples the longer to the shorter (FR-6.2.6).

4.5 Composite makers

Built from the above, and proven by the 282 Ideabook hints (FR-6.2.5b). Each returns Geometry.

CompositeConstruction
starOfCorners(center, r, n, steps, inner 0, twist 0, turn 0)tips tk on a circle of radius r; for each k a corner stitch from tk to tk+1 bending round ck, the centre when inner = 0, otherwise a point on a circle of radius inner at the half-angle between the tips, moved round by twist. n=4, inner 0: the four-pointed star; inner > 0: long thin points; twist: pinwheel blades.
polygonCornerStitch(corners, steps, full false)at every corner a corner stitch between the mid-points of its two edges, or with full the whole edges (corner to corner), leaving the round or elliptical holes of many boards.
segmentStitch(a1, a2, b1, b2, steps)pairwise on line(a1→a2) and line(b1→b2).
zigzagStitch(path, steps, colors)a corner stitch at every inner corner of a path.
offsetRings(center, r, n, rings, shrink, offset, drift)rings of nails each pairwise-joined to the next with an offset, the centres drifting: nested spirals.
pursuit(start, …)section 13.6.

4.6 Parametric sampling

V1 samples a parametric curve at Loops × 60 even steps in t (4,500 points at the default), all drawn and all searched (I-3). V2 samples adaptively.

sampleAdaptive(f, t0, t1, tol = 0.25 px, maxDepth = 14):
  start with 64 even steps in t
  for each interval [ta, tb]:
    m = f((ta+tb)/2);  e = distance from m to the chord f(ta)-f(tb)
    if e > tol and depth < maxDepth: split the interval and recurse
  then simplify (RDP, tol) and, if a nail count n is asked for, resample by length to n
DR-4.7For the default Parametrics settings, the sampled path shall have at most 720 points (V1's infrastructure limit) and draw within 0.5 px of the 4,500-point curve.
DR-4.8"Nails" (infrastructure) and "drawing" (the visible curve) may use different samplings of the same curve; a nail count is the owner's choice, a drawing tolerance is not.

4.7 Finders

A finder takes geometry and returns named points: finder(geometry, settings) → { [feature]: Point }.

FinderFeature namesRule
endsstart <path>, end <path>first and last points
middlesmid <path>half way by length
extremestop|bottom|left|right <path>by coordinate
lobeTipstip <path> #ka point farther from the curve's centre than its neighbours by at least 1.5 px within 3 points either side (V1 G-12), numbered by angle from the top, clockwise
cuspscusp <path> #ka turn sharper than 100° between consecutive segments
intersectionscross <pathA>.<pathB> #ksection 13.7
DR-4.9Feature numbering shall be stable under small changes: numbered by angle about the path's centroid from straight up, clockwise, so that moving a handle a little does not renumber.
DR-4.10Where two features coincide within 0.5 px, the more telling wins: intersection, cusp, tip, middle (V1 G-11).
DR-4.11A curve's intersections with itself shall be offered only when asked for (they run to thousands on a dense curve, V1 G-10).
DR-4.12The kernel's random source shall be a small seeded generator (Park–Miller, 16807 mod 231−1), so the same seed gives the same numbers in every browser.

4.8 Acceptance tests for the kernel

AT-4.1circle(n 36) + timesTable(k 2) gives 35 stitches whose envelope is a cardioid (checked against the cardioid's equation within 1 px at 36 sample angles).
AT-4.2corner(a, c, b, n 15) gives 16 stitches; stitch i joins a + (c−a)·i/15 to c + (b−c)·i/15.
AT-4.3jitter with seed 7, then seed 8, then seed 7 again: the first and third results are identical to the last bit.
AT-4.4Every kernel function, called with frozen arguments, does not throw and does not change them (DR-4.1).
AT-4.5pairwise with arms of 12 and 20 points joins 12 and returns one note naming both lengths.
AT-4.6Feature numbers of a rose's lobe tips do not change when the rose is turned by 1° (DR-4.9).
AT-4.7allPairs on 400 points (79,800 stitches) completes inside the budget of DR-17.1 or stops with the budget message (FR-6.18.2).
